title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Insurance Proceeds May Be Included in the Estate of the Insured

articles.content_en:
Reply on Whether Insurance Proceeds May Be Considered as Part of the Insured's Estate
(1987) Min Ta Zi No. 52
Higher People's Court of Hebei Province:
We have received your Request for Instructions, Ji Fa Min [1987] No. 1. According to the report: On May 26, 1986, Sun Wenxing, an individual tricycle motor driver from Nanjiao Village, Luancheng County, was transporting the consignor Zhang Xinguo and his goods (tin ingots) when a collision occurred with a train at the Douyu crossing of the Beijing-Guangzhou Railway, resulting in the deaths of both Sun Wenxing and Zhang Xinguo and the destruction of the tricycle motor. This accident shall be attributed to Sun Wenxing. Prior to his death, Sun Wenxing had taken out with the county insurance company not only vehicle damage insurance (with insurance proceeds of 3,500 yuan) but also personal accident insurance (with insurance proceeds of 5,000 yuan) and had designated a beneficiary. Now, Liang Jufen, the wife of consignor Zhang Xinguo, has filed a prosecution with the Luancheng County People's Court, demanding compensation from Guo Xiangrong, the wife of carrier Sun Wenxing.
After soliciting opinions from relevant departments, we hereby reply to your inquiry regarding whether personal insurance proceeds may be used as part of the insured's estate for compensation as follows:
(I) In accordance with the spirit of relevant provisions of China's insurance laws and regulations, whether personal insurance proceeds may be included in the insured's estate depends on whether the insured designated a beneficiary. If a beneficiary was designated, upon the death of the insured, the personal insurance proceeds shall be paid to the beneficiary; if no beneficiary was designated, upon the death of the insured, the personal insurance proceeds shall be treated as part of the estate and may be used to satisfy debts or provide compensation.
(II) Property insurance differs from personal insurance. There is no issue of designating a beneficiary in property insurance. Therefore, property insurance proceeds belong to the insured's estate. The vehicle damage insurance taken out by Sun Wenxing is property insurance and forms part of his estate, which may be used to satisfy debts or provide compensation.
In handling this case, the above principles shall be followed, with due attention to protecting the interests of creditors, and a fair and reasonable resolution shall be reached.
This reply is given.
March 24, 1988
